key_insight: A lightweight verifier trained on only a few labeled examples can filter and scale high-quality pseudo reasoning traces, making semi-supervised LLM reasoning competitive with much larger supervised datasets.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical low-label pipeline for building reasoning systems, reducing annotation cost while preserving performance for math and visual QA tasks.
method: Train a compact reasoning-correctness classifier from a small labeled set.
Generate intermediate reasoning traces with an LLM and score them with the verifier.
Use entropy-based confidence filtering to keep only reliable pseudo-labeled samples for fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: On Verifiable Math Problems (Orca-Math subset) and GQA with Visual Programming, the approach matches results that typically require 10–15× more labeled data.
watch_item: Performance depends on verifier quality and thresholding, so weak classifiers or poorly calibrated entropy filters can admit noise or discard useful reasoning traces.
paper_title: Scaling LLM Reasoning from Minimal Labels: A Semi-Supervised Framework with a Lightweight Verifier
